explorer.summary: The Sun is the star at the center of our solar system. Its gravity keeps every planet in orbit, and its light and heat power life on Earth.
facts: More than 99.8% of all the mass in the solar system is in the Sun.
About 1.3 million Earths could fit inside it.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.

scientist.summary: A G-type main-sequence star (G2V) fusing hydrogen into helium in its core at roughly 15 million K. Its effective surface temperature is about 5,772 K and its age is about 4.6 billion years.
facts: Holds 99.86% of the total mass of the solar system.
Luminosity of about 3.83 x 10^26 W.
Rotates differentially: about 25 days at the equator and about 35 days near the poles.

explorer.summary: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. It has no moons and almost no atmosphere.
facts: Daytime surface temperatures reach about 430 degrees C, while nights drop to about -180 degrees C.
A year on Mercury lasts only 88 Earth days.
Its surface is covered in craters, much like our Moon.

scientist.summary: A terrestrial planet in a 3:2 spin-orbit resonance, rotating three times for every two orbits. Its large iron core spans roughly 85% of the planet's radius, and it holds only a tenuous exosphere.
facts: One solar day lasts about 176 Earth days, twice its orbital period.
The orbital eccentricity of 0.206 is the highest of any planet.
The axial tilt of about 0.03 degrees is the smallest of any planet.

explorer.summary: Venus is the hottest planet, wrapped in thick clouds. It is similar in size to Earth, but its surface is a scorching, high-pressure desert.
facts: Venus spins backwards compared with most planets.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.
Surface temperatures of about 465 degrees C are hot enough to melt lead.

scientist.summary: A terrestrial planet with a dense carbon dioxide atmosphere and sulfuric acid clouds. A runaway greenhouse effect maintains a surface pressure of about 92 bar.
facts: Retrograde rotation with a sidereal period of about 243 days, longer than its 225-day orbit.
Its axial tilt of about 177 degrees reflects the retrograde spin.
Nearly circular orbit with an eccentricity of 0.0068.

explorer.summary: Earth is our home and the only place we know of that has life. Liquid water covers most of its surface.
facts: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water.
Earth has one natural satellite, the Moon.
Earth's tilt is what gives us the seasons.

scientist.summary: A terrestrial planet with a nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere, a global magnetic field, and active plate tectonics. Orbital data shown is for the Earth-Moon barycenter.
facts: The atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.
The axial tilt of 23.44 degrees drives seasonal insolation changes.
The orbital eccentricity of 0.0167 puts perihelion in early January.

explorer.summary: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite. It always shows us the same face as it circles our planet.
facts: It is likely the result of a giant collision early in Earth's history.
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth, about 3.8 centimeters each year.
Its gravity causes the ocean tides.

scientist.summary: Earth's only natural satellite, in synchronous rotation. Its mass is about 1.2% of Earth's, and its orbit is inclined about 5.1 degrees to the ecliptic.
facts: Tidally locked, so its rotation period equals its orbital period of 27.32 days.
The orbital eccentricity of 0.055 causes visible libration.
The orbit's line of nodes regresses with a period of about 18.6 years.

explorer.summary: Mars is a cold, dusty desert world. Its red color comes from rusty iron in the soil.
facts: Olympus Mons, a volcano about 22 km tall, is the tallest in the solar system.
Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.
A day on Mars is just a little longer than a day on Earth.

scientist.summary: A terrestrial planet with a thin carbon dioxide atmosphere at roughly 0.6% of Earth's surface pressure. Past liquid water is recorded in its geology.
facts: Rotation period of 24 h 37 min and an axial tilt of about 25 degrees give Earth-like seasons.
Valles Marineris stretches about 4,000 km.
Orbital eccentricity of 0.093 makes seasons uneven between hemispheres.

explorer.summary: Jupiter is the largest planet. It is a huge ball of gas with colorful stripes and storms.
facts: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.
The Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth that has lasted for centuries.
A day on Jupiter lasts only about 10 hours.

scientist.summary: A gas giant composed mostly of hydrogen and helium, with the strongest planetary magnetic field in the solar system. Its rapid rotation produces banded zonal winds.
facts: Mean radius of about 11 Earth radii and a mass of about 318 Earth masses.
Sidereal rotation period of roughly 9.9 hours.
Orbital period of 11.86 years at 5.2 AU, with more than 90 known moons.

explorer.summary: Saturn is famous for its bright rings, which are made of countless pieces of ice and rock.
facts: Saturn is less dense than water, so it would float in a giant bathtub.
It has hundreds of known moons, including the large moon Titan.
The rings are wide but extremely thin.

scientist.summary: A gas giant of hydrogen and helium with a ring system of mostly water ice. The main rings extend hundreds of thousands of kilometers but are typically only about ten meters thick.
facts: Mean density of about 0.69 g/cm3, the lowest of any planet.
A persistent hexagonal jet stream surrounds the north pole.
Orbital period of 29.4 years and a rotation period of about 10.7 hours.

explorer.summary: Uranus is a pale blue-green planet that rolls around the Sun tipped on its side.
facts: Its axis is tilted nearly 98 degrees, so it spins on its side.
Its blue-green color comes from methane in the atmosphere.
One year on Uranus lasts about 84 Earth years.

scientist.summary: An ice giant with a hydrogen, helium, and methane atmosphere over a mantle of water, ammonia, and methane ices. It rotates retrograde on an axis tilted about 98 degrees.
facts: Holds the coldest recorded planetary atmosphere, with a minimum near 49 K.
Each pole spends about 21 years in continuous sunlight, then 21 years in darkness.
Sidereal rotation period of about 17.2 hours, retrograde.

explorer.summary: Neptune is a deep blue planet at the edge of the solar system. It is cold, dark, and very windy.
facts: Winds on Neptune can blow faster than 2,000 kilometers per hour.
It was found in 1846 using math before it was ever seen through a telescope.
One year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years.

scientist.summary: An ice giant with an atmosphere of hydrogen, helium, and methane. It radiates more energy than it receives from the Sun and has the fastest sustained winds of any planet.
facts: Its large moon Triton orbits retrograde and is likely a captured Kuiper belt object.
The planet completed its first full orbit since discovery in 2011.
Orbital period of about 164.8 years at 30.1 AU.
